placement:
ACCIDENT SCENE. The poop is near the middle of the frame, and the investigation has gone wrong. Where this conflicts with the poses, gas-mask rules, or gaze rules in sections 2, 5, 6, 11, 12, and 14, this section wins.

The Hazardous-Material Specialist has passed out on the pavement on the right side of the poop. It lies on its side with its feet sticking out and its head resting on the ground. It looks unconscious, not injured: no blood, no visible harm, feathers intact, still wearing its yellow vest. Its gas mask has come off and lies on the pavement nearby.

The equipment line (the case, the camera on its tripod, and the detector) sits on the left side of the poop. The Curious Investigator has left its post and is stepping toward the camera, in front of the equipment line, looking directly into the lens. Its pose and expression stay natural and pigeon-like, never human.

The poop stays clearly visible in the middle, inside the evidence markers.
lighting:
### Floodlight

This photograph was taken at night. Include a compact portable LED work floodlight on a small folding stand among the equipment near the first pigeon, aimed at the investigation area.

The floodlight casts a localized pool of bright, slightly cool light over the poop, the evidence markers, and both pigeons, with realistic falloff, hard-edged shadows, and specular highlights on the equipment. Outside that pool, keep the original night lighting of the photograph unchanged.

The floodlight should look like real professional field equipment, clean and realistically maintained.
